title.narrative: MMR 100253- EQR DEC Collective Initiatives - Inle Lake

description.narrative: The proposal builds on global discourse on Humanitarian Reset1 and local experience in EQ Emergency Response and Recovery Programme of ActionAid and PLAN. _x000d_ _x000d_ The current humanitarian system lacks: _x000d_ _x000d_ • Community-led decision-making _x000d_ • Long-term resilience planning _x000d_ • Transparent, accessible information _x000d_ • Inclusive funding models _x000d_ _x000d_ Inle Lake is located in an ecologically fragile zone in Southern Shan State, is particularly vulnerable to multiple hazards including floods, storms, and earthquakes. In 2025, communities already affected by the earthquake faced additional hardship due to heavy rains and rising floodwater. Many were forced to live in makeshift temporary shelters, as reconstruction of damaged homes remained incomplete. The people of Inle endured a double burden—loss of livelihoods from both the earthquake and flooding. _x000d_ The Inle Youth Volunteer Network (IYVN) exemplifies how locally driven leadership can be a more effective, impactful, and resource-efficient model for emergency response than traditional external aid. While community efforts in the emergency response are highly valued, their energy and commitment can be harnessed for longer-term recovery. The experience of Inle and its surrounding communities offers a compelling case for reimagining humanitarian action through a locally led lens. However, these groups face challenges in securing funding for these sustained efforts, as the current funding model does not allow informal volunteer groups to receive support for long-term recovery and resilience-building programs. To address this issue, this project aims to set up system of a Recovery and Learning Centre with a funding provision to support Disaster Preparedness, Response, Anticipatory Actions. Together, the Resource Centre and DPRF form a resilient, locally anchored system that not only responds to disasters but also prepares communities to anticipate and mitigate future risks. Their synergy offers a compelling blueprint for inclusive, sustainable humanitarian action _x000d_ _x000d_ Objectives_x000d_ _x000d_ Train youth and women volunteers as Agents of Change (AoCs) _x000d_ _x000d_ 1.Empower Local Leadership and Community-Led Response_x000d_ _x000d_ 2.Coordinate Inclusive and Transparent Humanitarian Action _x000d_ _x000d_ 3.Promote Long-Term Resilience and Ecological Restoration _x000d_ _x000d_ 4. Facilitate Research, Learning, and Advocacy_x000d_ _x000d_ ActionAid Myanmar (AAM) and Plan International are co-travellers in the journey to strengthen localization in Myanmar. Both organizations bring extensive experience and proven capacities in working with the most vulnerable communities across various disaster contexts. Their shared commitment to locally led humanitarian action forms the foundation of a collective initiative designed to empower communities and build long-term resilience. _x000d_ Strategic Collaboration _x000d_ AAM and Plan will co-lead this collective initiative, pooling resources to: _x000d_ • Support community-generated village recovery plans _x000d_ • Enhance the capacity of youth fellows in the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) _x000d_ • Establish robust accountability mechanisms to ensure transparency and responsiveness to affected communities _x000d_ • Together, AAM and Plan will oversee the management of the Disaster Preparedness and Response nd (DPRF). In consultation with local organizations and business groups, they will co-develop the governance framework and operational systems for the DPRF, ensuring it is community-managed, transparent, and responsive. _x000d_ _x000d_ Plan International _x000d_ • Support youth leadership development initiatives, such as inclusive disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, climate resilience and anticipatory action at schools and their communities _x000d_ • Strengthen gender, disability inclusion and child rights programming within the broader recovery and resilience framework
